content: ABCD2, also known as ATP-binding cassette sub-family D member 2, is a membrane pump or transporter protein encoded by the ABCD2 gene in humans. Function The protein encoded by the ABCD2 gene belongs to the ATP-binding cassette (ABC) transporter superfamily. ABC proteins are responsible for transporting various molecules across both extracellular and intracellular membranes. The ABC gene family is categorized into seven distinct subfamilies: ABC1, MDR/TAP, MRP, ALD, OABP, GCN20, and White. ABCD2 is a member of the ALD subfamily, which is specifically involved in the peroxisomal import of fatty acids and/or fatty acyl-CoAs into the organelle. All known peroxisomal ABC transporters are half-transporters, meaning they require a partner half-transporter molecule to form a functional transporter. These functional transporters can be either homodimeric or heterodimeric in structure. While the exact function of this peroxisomal membrane protein remains unknown, it is hypothesized to act as a dimerization partner for ABCD1 or other peroxisomal ABC transporters. Clinical Significance Mutations in the ABCD2 gene have been identified in patients with adrenoleukodystrophy, a severe demyelinating disease. This gene has been proposed as a candidate modifier gene, potentially explaining the significant variability observed in the phenotypes of adrenoleukodystrophy. Additionally, ABCD2 is considered a candidate gene for a complement group associated with Zellweger syndrome, a genetically heterogeneous disorder affecting peroxisomal biogenesis.
